Vijayapura in Crl.Misc.No.532/2024 (Crime No.36/2024 registered by Jalanagar Police Station,

sentences.text:
02. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State and the learned counsel for the respondents No.2 and 3.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:5988 03.

The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint filed by the petitioner before the Jalanagar Police Station, Vijayapura the police have registered the FIR against the respondents Nos.2 and 3 - accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No.36/2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468 and 471 read with Section 34 of IPC, alleging that they had created the fake documents and placed before the Registrar of Societies.
Upon registering the FIR, the accused had apprehending their arrest in the hands of the police, they had approached the learned Sessions Judge for granting anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the learned Sessions Judge, granted anticipatory bail by the impugned order, with the conditions as under:-
a) They shall not hamper, tamper and threat the prosecution witnesses.
b) They shall surrender before the concerned Police Station, within 15 days from the date of order.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:5988 c) They shall co-operate with the I.O. in the investigation.
d) They shall regularly attend the Court without fail.
e) They shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court without prior permission.

f) The petitioners/accused shall mark their attendance before the concerned police station on every fortnightly Sunday in between 10.00 a.m. to 06.00 p.m. to till filing of the final report or for six months whichever is earlier.

sentences.text: The petitioners/accused and surety shall furnish their current residential address proof along with recent passport size photos and mobile numbers to the investigating officer.
In case of violation of any one of the above mentioned conditions, the prosecution is at liberty to move for cancellation of bail.
Accordingly, the respondents No.2 and 3 are said to be surrendered before the police and obtained the bail.
They are said to be issued legal notice to the police through their advocate.

Hence,
the petitioner / complainant is before this Court for canceling the bail mainly on the ground that the respondents No.2 and 3 threatening the complainant and not allowing the police to investigate the matter, they issued the legal notice and threatening the police officer and they are not able to investigate the matter properly.
Hence, the petitioner / complainant has filed this petition for canceling the bail.
05. The learned counsel for the petitioner / complainant contended that the respondents No.2 and 3 have not complied the condition of the Trial Court.
They are threatening the witnesses and not allowing the Investigating Officer to investigate the matter.
Hence, prayed for canceling the bail.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents No.2 and 3 has submitted that as per the Court order the respondents No.2 and 3 had surrendered before the Court for seeking the bail, but the police officers have not accepting the sureties and continuously made to sit in the police station and not accepting the sureties and not releasing the accused persons on anticipatory bail.

Therefore,
the respondents No.2 and 3 forced to issue legal notice through their advocate.
Thereafter, surety was accepted and now the police have investigated the matter and they have filed the charge- sheet.
The summons have been issued to the respondents No.2 and 3 to appear before the Magistrate.
Such being the case, absolutely, there is no grounds made out for canceling the bail.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the petition.

07. The learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State has been instructed to get the report of the Investigating Officer, whether the NC: 2024:KHC-K:5988 respondents No.2 and 3 have complied the conditions imposed by the Sessions Judge while granting the bail.
Accordingly, the report of the Investigating Officer has been submitted to the Court.
The same is placed on record.

08. Having been heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, it reveals that of course the complainant had filed complaint to the police against the respondents No.2 and 3, the police had registered FIR and investigated the matter.
The respondents No.2 and 3 have already approached the Sessions Judge.
The learned Sessions Judge had granted the bail by impugned order.
The Sessions Judge while considering the dispute between the parties and later granted the anticipatory bail on satisfaction of grounds urged by the learned counsel for the accused.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the respondents No.2 and 3 were surrendered before the police and the police officer especially the Investigating Officer not accepted the surety and not complied the condition of the bail order passed by the Sessions Judge.
Therefore, the respondents No.2 and 3 are constrained to issue legal notice to the concerned police for accepting the surety as per the order passed by the Session Judge.

The learned counsel brought to the notice of this Court that the prayer of advocate's notice which clearly reveals to accept the surety bond of his clients and to comply the order of the Sessions Judge.

On perusal of the said legal notice, this Court do not find any threaten made by the accused persons to the Investigating Officer, but they requested to accept the surety bond as per the conditions imposed by the Sessions Judge.

10. That apart the report sent by the Investigating Officer, dated 13.08.2024 through the High Court Government Pleader, wherein it is stated that all the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5988 conditions of the bail has been complied by the accused persons.

It is also seen from the records that the police have already investigated the matter and the charge-sheet is also filed before the Magistrate which is numbered as C.C.No.1462/2024.
11.
Such being the case, I am of the view that the police have already investigated the matter, filed the charge-sheet and summons were also issued to the respondents No.2 and 3.

There is no grounds made out by the petitioner / complainant to show that the accused persons have violated any condition of the bail or the order passed by the Sessions Judge was perverse, capricious or not properly appreciated the documents while granting the bail, in order to cancel the bail.
12.

That apart, another contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner / complainant that the accused persons threatened the petitioner / complainant, but till the date no complaint has been filed before the police or any complaint made to the concerned Court to show that the accused persons were threatened them for withdrawing the complaint for compromise.

Such being the case, I do not find any error in granting the anticipatory bail or there is no ground made out for canceling the bail granted by the Sessions Judge, by exercising the power under Section 439 (2) of Cr.P.C.
This Court is well aware about the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the bail is a rule, rejection is a exception.
In anticipatory bail, it is also held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that granting bail is rule, rejection is a exception.

Even if any bail Akbar Patil vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177236009/
5 conditions are violated then the petitioner / complainant could have approached the same Court for canceling the bail.

ORDER I.
The petition is dismissed.
